## Goal

Make genuine TDK CLI package usage discoverable through GitHub's public dependency graph. Do not add package declarations or manifests solely to affect a metric.

## Baseline

The OpenSpec proposal records **0 dependents as of 20 October 2026**. This is the supplied proposal baseline; the live dependents page was not independently readable during this audit. Re-check it after confirmed consumer changes reach default branches.

## Audit snapshot (20 October 2026)

All primary candidates below are public and active. Repository trees, root package metadata and READMEs were inspected. “Documented CLI usage” does not by itself mean a local npm dependency; several projects currently expect a global or standalone TDK CLI install.

| Repository | Current evidence | Disposition |
|---|---|---|

| [tdk-saas-starter](https://github.com/tdk-landscape/tdk-saas-starter) | Root `package.json` + `bun.lock`; 6 nested service manifests; no core dependency | Candidate only if local CLI dependency and invocation are introduced coherently |

| [tdk-agent-stack](https://github.com/tdk-landscape/tdk-agent-stack) | 2 service manifests; no root manifest/lock; README documents TDK setup | No local package dependency; requires a deliberate local-install workflow to change |

| [tdk-docker-compose-example](https://github.com/tdk-landscape/tdk-docker-compose-example) | No Node manifest/lock; README runs CLI inside Compose | Likely exception; audit its container image and document rationale |

Secondary audit-only repos: `tdk-skills` (agent instructions, no root manifest), `awesome-tdk-framework` (curated links), `tdk-website` and `tdk-landscape.github.io` (docs/install site, no root manifest), `tdk-demo-animation` (assets), `tdk-cli-releases` (release artifacts/global-install docs), `tdk-service-definitions` (AJV validation package and service registry, no core dependency), `tdk-import` (separate npm package; core command is invoked by the TDK CLI), and `tdk-app` (uses an installed CLI, no core dependency). `tdk-labs`, `platform`, and `tdk-cli-extensions` were not identified as first-wave examples/starters; review if their maintained workflows directly install the published core package.

## Why
The repository declares pnpm as its package manager but tracks both `pnpm-lock.yaml` and a root `package-lock.json`. Multiple lockfiles can produce different dependency graphs across tools and contributors.

## Scope
Make pnpm the single package manager represented in version control.

## Acceptance criteria
- Remove the root `package-lock.json`.
- Ignore `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, and Bun lockfiles at the repository root.
- Add a small CI check that exactly one supported root lockfile is tracked.
- Keep `pnpm-lock.yaml` unchanged unless an existing consistency error requires regeneration.
- Document `pnpm@10.13.1` as the required installer.

Do not upgrade dependencies.

items.body:
<!-- keron-architecture-20261025:E07.02 -->

Package managers can run concurrently, batching can reorder dependent resources, and elevation currently moves writes after unprivileged steps.

## Work order

Start after #139 (E07.01). Stage: **Core**. Follow the numeric Order field in [keron](https://github.com/users/icepuma/projects/8).

Parent epic: #138 (E07).

Technical prerequisites: #139 (E07.01), #123 (E05), #130 (E06).

## Scope

- Use one serial dependency scheduler for native resources and delegated provider actions.
- Batch only operations that preserve the declared ordering and can report outcomes for each resource; otherwise use individual operations.
- Stop dependents after failed or unresolved prerequisites. Preserve the graph order across any privilege path that #101 (E01) still permits.
- Integrate #123 (E05) re-observation of every node, including NoOp, and final verification after delegated actions.
- Report verification as an interval, not one global instant or a promise against later external writers.

## Acceptance checks

- [ ] Fake brew and cargo logs never overlap and respect interleaved file dependencies.
- [ ] A failed prerequisite prevents its consumer from running.
- [ ] If privilege support remains reachable, a privileged producer is not deferred past its unprivileged consumer.
- [ ] Approval-window changes to NoOp resources fail verification; final checks include resources modified by later commands.

## Evidence

items.title: Reject build-time dependency graph regeneration in currently locked image consumers
items.body:
## Parent

Part of #94 (https://github.com/gregwebs/agent-vm-images/issues/94).

## What to build

Existing dsh, Pi, bridge and plugin builds consume reviewed committed dependency inputs; changing a version requires a maintenance proposal rather than build-local lock generation.

## Binding policy

Scope: maintained base/standard and every checked-in example. A pinned image input has a reviewed, committed selection and content identity; exact versions alone do not suffice. Only packages from official Debian apt repositories may float, with normal apt authentication retained. This exception does not cover parent images, NodeSource, GitHub CLI or other third-party inputs. Verify upstream signatures/attestations where available against an explicit trusted identity; document reviewed hash-only exceptions. Pinning does not establish that a release is safe.

Ordinary builds only verify committed pins: no latest lookup, graph regeneration, checksum refresh, silent fallback or image-owned first-use downloads. Explicit maintenance may regenerate hashes/locks/digests into reviewed proposals; never auto-adopt or auto-merge. User/project-triggered installs are outside the guarantee. Byte-identical outputs and an owned artifact mirror are not required.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For ordinary image builds, accept empty/equal compatibility slots only and reject a different exact version before a manager/network call, source mutation or partial installation. Maintain the already equal-only plugin behavior.
- [ ] Do not wait for pnpm migration: enforce the guard on the current dsh pnpm and Pi/bridge npm paths. Current Pi 1.3.0 and bridge already have fully hashed committed npm locks; preserve those pins and do not introduce a redundant migration.
- [ ] Keep explicit developer maintenance capable of automatically regenerating hashes/locks after validation. Separate that authorized entrypoint from ordinary build preparation; no environment flag that silently re-enables build-time resolution.
- [ ] Amend ADR 0003's deliberately retained changed-selection build interface and related docs/tests explicitly. Its graph comparator remains useful for reviewed maintenance; this policy does not require hand-editing locks or prohibit intentional reviewed transitive updates.
- [ ] Coordinate with the pinning amendments on #63/#64/#53 so later migrations preserve the guard. This ticket has no blocker on those migrations or on #53.
- [ ] Add mutation tests for changed exact version, dist-tags/ranges, modified committed lock/hash, alternate manager entrypoints and attempted refresh during builds. Prove zero manager/network preparation on rejected selections and positive frozen installs on committed selections.
- [ ] Retain native amd64/arm64 current-product runtime/certification/egress gates; move changed-version build acceptance cases into explicit staged-maintenance tests instead of dropping coverage.

## Source references

At commit `24d78572b4998cb70116398e08482adc8fb543cf` (baseline references, not unversioned implementation promises):

- [`images/tools/dsh/prepare-lock.sh`](https://github.com/gregwebs/agent-vm-images/blob/24d78572b4998cb70116398e08482adc8fb543cf/images/tools/dsh/prepare-lock.sh)
- [`images/tools/pi/prepare-lock.sh`](https://github.com/gregwebs/agent-vm-images/blob/24d78572b4998cb70116398e08482adc8fb543cf/images/tools/pi/prepare-lock.sh)
- [`images/tools/pi/bridge/prepare-lock.sh`](https://github.com/gregwebs/agent-vm-images/blob/24d78572b4998cb70116398e08482adc8fb543cf/images/tools/pi/bridge/prepare-lock.sh)
- [`images/standard/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/gregwebs/agent-vm-images/blob/24d78572b4998cb70116398e08482adc8fb543cf/images/standard/Dockerfile)
- [`docs/adr/0003-dsh-graph-freeze.md`](https://github.com/gregwebs/agent-vm-images/blob/24d78572b4998cb70116398e08482adc8fb543cf/docs/adr/0003-dsh-graph-freeze.md)
- [`script/test/standard-node-consumers.sh`](https://github.com/gregwebs/agent-vm-images/blob/24d78572b4998cb70116398e08482adc8fb543cf/script/test/standard-node-consumers.sh)

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

Here's a brief migration guide that I came up with while working on https://github.com/oss-review-toolkit/ort/pull/9073:

1. Refactor existing code so that all metadata for a dependency is available in a single data class, let's name it `D`.
2. Implement a `DependencyHandler<D>` that returns various ORT model classes for that data class `D`.
3. In the specific package manager class, create a `val graphBuilder = DependencyGraphBuilder(...)` member variable that takes an instance of that `DependencyHandler`.
4. In `resolveDependencies()`, call `graphBuilder.addDependencies(..)` for the dependencies.
5. Change creating a `Project` from setting `scopeDependencies` to setting `scopeNames = graphBuilder.scopesFor(projectId)`.
6. Change the returned `ProjectAnalyzerResult` to take an `emptySet()` as packages.
7. Override `createPackageManagerResult()` with `PackageManagerResult(projectResults, graphBuilder.build(), graphBuilder.packages())`.
8. In existing tests that call `resolveSingleProject()`, ensure to pass `resolveScopes = true`.

## Queue reconciliation — 2026-10-20

The ten-child table below is the canonical package-command plan. Duplicate chain #8333/#8335/#8338/#8340/#8342 is closed in favor of #8331/#8339, #8332, #8337/#8336, #8341/#8334/#8343, and #8344 respectively. The ready transaction tip is #8330; declared/active planning and config/cache foundations retain their separate ready tips. Closing duplicates satisfies no implementation prerequisite.

---

# package manager: add dependency commands, graph inspection, vendoring, and offline policy

> Decision: filed with explicit foundational sequencing as
> [#6957](https://github.com/JoNil-Botta/typelisp/issues/6957) on 2026-08-30.

## What problem does this solve?

TypeLisp already has local and GitHub-hosted dependencies, exact revisions, a
lockfile, deterministic cache layout, and update-lock behavior. Users still have to
edit S-expression manifests by hand, inspect lockfiles manually, and infer why
a package was selected or fetched. There is no command-level offline/frozen
contract or supported way to vendor a locked graph.

These gaps make the existing deterministic package foundation harder to use
than it needs to be and complicate hermetic CI.

## Describe the solution

Add a coherent package command suite against the current exact-pin model:

- add and remove dependencies with explicit local/GitHub source selectors and
  the general Git selector once that focused source-model follow-up lands;
- update one dependency or the graph under explicit lock policy;
- fetch without building;
- tree with normal/inverted/duplicate/package filtering;
- metadata as stable machine-readable project/graph data;
- vendor to a deterministic directory plus generated source replacement
  configuration;
- offline, locked, and frozen modes with distinct documented meanings;
- cache location/status/verify/prune commands, with `verify` using the focused
  lock-to-source integrity contract and prune always explicit and recoverable.

All manifest edits should be parsed, semantically validated, formatted
canonically, and atomically replaced. Lock edits must use #6966's
application-owned direct dependency graph and the focused atomic-update
contract. Comments and unrelated fields must not be silently destroyed.

## Sequencing

Treat this as the user-facing command layer, not the place to redesign package
correctness implicitly:

1. Enforce #6966 so library artifacts reject normal TypeLisp package
   dependencies and the root application owns every normal package edge.
2. Confine fetched packages to their locked checkout,
   canonicalize/verify cached source, and make lock replacement atomic and
   conflict-aware.
3. Settle the single-package target, native-link, and exact-pin dependency-
   context models before freezing command flags or metadata fields that expose
   them.
4. Then implement the command suite in reusable slices: read-only graph/cache
   inspection, fetch/offline policy, manifest mutation and selective update,
   and finally vendoring/pruning.

An early read-only slice may land once its underlying graph schema is stable.
Mutation, update, and vendor commands must not create parallel lock/cache edit
paths while the foundational transactions are still unsettled.

## Selfhost implementation target

- package manifest CST/edit support and canonical formatter
- package source, lock, cache, and graph modules
- src package CLI dispatch and common output events
- tools/tests for local and temporary git repositories
- docs/packages.md and command reference

## Acceptance criteria

- add/remove/update produce valid deterministic manifests and lockfiles and
  preserve unrelated comments/sections.
- fetch followed by frozen/offline build performs no network or git remote
  operation.
- locked mode fails rather than modifying an absent/stale lock; frozen also
  forbids network and source mutation.
- tree explains aliases, source identity, exact commit, duplicate versions,
  and dependency path; inverted queries identify dependents.
- metadata is schema-versioned and includes packages, targets, dependencies,
  resolved sources, cfg/profile inputs, and artifact roots.
- vendor copies only verified locked source, writes deterministic mapping
  metadata, and permits a clean-cache offline build.
- Commands are safe under concurrent invocation and recover atomically from
  interruption.
- Credentials and remote URLs containing secrets are redacted from output,
  locks, diagnostics, and event streams.
- Linux and Windows path/layout parity is tested.

## Alternatives and non-goals

This proposal does not require a registry or semantic-version solver. Delivering
it first improves today's exact-pin workflow and supplies graph/edit primitives
that any future resolver or registry work can reuse. Cache pruning must never be
an implicit side effect of build.

## Related work

Closed #1157, #1159, #1993, #2002, #2549, and #2892 established sources, lock
replay, cache, and link inputs. Focused follow-ups own locked-checkout
verification, general Git sources, package targets, native-link propagation,
dependency contexts, direct root-lock behavior, atomic updates, and fetched-
path confinement. #6966 removes the need for a transitive root-lock schema.
This issue should expose those contracts rather than invent competing ones.


## Current focused dependency graph (2026-09-29, worker 5)

Research/decomposition is complete against main `4f644b48f0e6338628755e58dff6c34607fbaf16`. The finite implementation leaves below preserve the entire command-suite scope. This issue remains the terminal acceptance owner and is blocked on them; filing the leaves does not claim the commands are implemented.

Current main has build/run `--locked`/`--update-lock`, atomic lock replacement (#6984), shallow root-owned normal graphs (#6966), fetched-path confinement, and native-link propagation (#6982). It has no tree/metadata/fetch/add/remove/update/vendor/cache commands or offline/frozen policy. `format_cst.tl` already retains comment trivia and should be extended by the mutation leaf rather than copied.

| Slice | Implementation owner | Direct prerequisites |
|---|---|---|
| Coherent manifest/lock edits and interruption recovery | #8330 | None open; extend landed #6984 and its production reader/writer boundary |
| Read-only tree, inverted/duplicates/package filters and native-link-plan view | #8331 | #7098, #6981; #6982 is landed |
| Machine metadata: graph/targets/config/artifacts and ordered native-link plan | #8339 | #8331, #6981, #7098, #6952, #6963 |
| Fetch and distinct offline/locked/frozen policy through commands/workers | #8332 | #7098, #8191, #6973 |
| Comment-preserving CST add/remove with coherent complete lock edits | #8337 | #8330, #8332, #7095, #7096 |
| Selective/whole declared remote-pin update | #8336 | #8330, #8332, #7096, #8191 |
| Verified vendor bundle and deterministic source replacements | #8341 | #8332, #6973, #7245, #6963 |
| Read-only cache location/status/source verification | #8334 | #6973, #6952, #6963 |
| Explicit recoverable prune/restore with live-consumer protection | #8343 | #8334, #8332, #6973, #7245 |
| General Git/subdirectory command adapter | #8344 | #6980 plus #8337/#8331/#8339/#8332/#8336/#8341/#8334 |

The first nine leaves are Next-horizon package correctness/tooling work and do not wait for #6980. Only #8344 consumes that Later-horizon native Git/source/subdirectory chain. #7098 already depends on #7095-#7097. #6973 owns canonical source-inventory admission; #7245 owns publication/cleanup, not source schema. Closed #6984/#6966/#6982 are invariants, not open blockers.

### Resolved command contracts

- Locks are declaration-wide, including inactive target/test rows; availability/build/TLCI/link work follows only the selected active plan. Inspections never fetch or mutate to make an unavailable source appear resolved.
- `--locked` is read-only lock validation but may fetch active exact sources. `--offline` forbids remote/network operations and resolves only locally provable pins; a corrupt source fails without online repair. `--frozen` adds locked validation and forbids source-cache/replacement mutation, while permitting ordinary build artifacts. Frozen retains full source verification.
- Add/remove preserve comment text and unrelated fields through the existing CST; manifest/lock pair publication uses #8330's shared guard and interrupted-edit recovery. Two independent atomic file writes are not sufficient for a coherent pair.
- Selective update refreshes exactly one declared remote pin and retains every unrelated row. Whole update refreshes the complete declared set; neither silently rewrites manifest source selectors.
- Tree and metadata reuse the landed native-link ordering/provenance model (`build-package-graph-link-inputs`, `SourceToolLinkOrigins`, `.runtime-inputs` native-link triples); Linux dependency-group boundaries remain explicit. Metadata reuses #6952's schema-1 pre-1.0 convention and #6963's effective value origins.
- Vendor publishes verified inventory and deterministic relative replacement mappings for every declared remote row; local paths remain explicit local prerequisites. A clean-cache offline/frozen build proves replacement consumption, TLCI provenance and native-input confinement.
- Cache queries/verify are read-only. Prune is explicit dry-run/apply, protects complete-lock references and active source-use leases, quarantines recoverably, and makes irreversible purge separately explicit.

### Terminal acceptance retained here

Keep this issue open until all original acceptance criteria pass together: complete human and machine command workflows, deterministic comment-preserving manifest/lock results, coherent concurrent/interrupted edits and source publication, zero forbidden remote/source mutations under the documented policies, ordered graph/link explanations, clean-cache vendored replay, credential redaction, Linux/Windows parity, docs/help/completion, and full unchanged required CI/bootstrap coverage. Every leaf specifies invalid-input, boundary and interaction tests; consumers must share the same planner/configuration/transactions rather than adding parallel paths.

Updated 2026-09-29 (worker 5): filed the ten finite implementation leaves, made #8330 ready because it has no open prerequisite, blocked the remaining leaves on explicit links, and replaced the prior pending decomposition. No registry, semver, workspaces, publishing or nested library dependency scope was added.

items.title: Add apk package manager commands
items.body:
Version: `git-pkgs/managers` current `main` at [`241e284`](https://github.com/git-pkgs/managers/commit/241e28416122e0c1f79aa5c590fe4f154e0a58ce).

Trying to build Alpine package operations after registering the embedded definitions currently returns `unknown manager: apk`:

```go
_, err := tr.BuildCommand("apk", "add", managers.CommandInput{
	Args: map[string]string{"package": "curl", "version": "8.14.1-r2"},
})
```

Add an `apk` definition for Alpine's system package manager. Include `definitions/apk.yaml`, captured version and command help under `references/apk`, translator tests, and Docker coverage as described in the [new manager contribution guide](https://github.com/git-pkgs/managers/blob/241e28416122e0c1f79aa5c590fe4f154e0a58ce/CONTRIBUTING.md#L3-L20).

The command mapping should follow apk's own command and file formats:

- Use `apk add` and `apk del` for package constraints. The [`apk-world(5)` package specification](https://github.com/alpinelinux/apk-tools/blob/3174f53b7de3676c747fee9097ef6427fb5a8060/doc/apk-world.5.scd#L7-L62) covers exact versions such as `curl=8.14.1-r2` and tagged repositories such as `curl@edge`.
- Use `apk list --installed` for `list`, `apk list --upgradable` for `outdated`, and `apk upgrade [packages]` for `update`. [`apk update` only refreshes repository indexes](https://github.com/alpinelinux/apk-tools/blob/3174f53b7de3676c747fee9097ef6427fb5a8060/doc/apk-update.8.scd#L7-L17), so it should not be exposed as a package update.
- `apk dot --installed` can provide raw dependency graph output for `resolve`; the command supports the shared query filters documented by [`apk-query(8)`](https://github.com/alpinelinux/apk-tools/blob/3174f53b7de3676c747fee9097ef6427fb5a8060/doc/apk-query.8.scd#L7-L65).
- Do not advertise `path` from `apk info --contents`. That command returns every owned file, not one package directory.

The generic `install` operation needs a safe definition because it has no package argument. [`apk fix`](https://github.com/alpinelinux/apk-tools/blob/3174f53b7de3676c747fee9097ef6427fb5a8060/doc/apk-fix.8.scd#L7-L24) repairs or reinstalls packages, so it should not be used as an install alias. Leave `install` unsupported unless the operation can reconcile a supplied world file without changing the existing API contract.

Repository flags need a small translator change. Apk requires [global options before the command](https://github.com/alpinelinux/apk-tools/blob/3174f53b7de3676c747fee9097ef6427fb5a8060/doc/apk.8.scd#L7-L26), while the current translator [adds the command, positional arguments, and then dynamic flags](https://github.com/git-pkgs/managers/blob/241e28416122e0c1f79aa5c590fe4f154e0a58ce/translator.go#L89-L123). Add support for pre-command flags so repository selection is emitted as `apk --repository URL add PACKAGE`. The upstream [`apk-repositories(5)` examples](https://github.com/alpinelinux/apk-tools/blob/3174f53b7de3676c747fee9097ef6427fb5a8060/doc/apk-repositories.5.scd#L48-L67) show repository configuration files that can be used as fixtures.

Commands that change the system normally require elevated permissions. The current [`Command` schema](https://github.com/git-pkgs/managers/blob/241e28416122e0c1f79aa5c590fe4f154e0a58ce/definitions/schema.go#L36-L45) does not expose this to callers. Add per-command privilege metadata and keep `sudo` out of generated commands so the caller controls elevation.

Tests should cover exact versions, repository tags and URLs, flag placement, installed and upgradable listings, package-specific and system upgrades, dependency graph output, and privilege metadata. Apk is [non-interactive by default](https://github.com/alpinelinux/apk-tools/blob/3174f53b7de3676c747fee9097ef6427fb5a8060/doc/apk.8.scd#L19-L26), so the definition should not add a nonexistent `-y` flag.

items.title: Reconcile dependency security and package-manager policy
items.body:
## Problem

The repository's dependency security workflow is ambiguous: Dependabot is configured for Yarn, while the repository also contains npm package metadata and lock state, and historical Issue 13 refers to a vulnerable request package that is not a direct dependency in the current package manifest.

## Evidence

.github/dependabot.yml monitors the Yarn ecosystem. The current direct dependency list does not include request, so the historical alert must be reconciled against the complete lockfile graph before it is considered resolved.

## Proposed scope

Choose and document one canonical install workflow, align Dependabot with it, inspect both lockfiles for drift or reachable vulnerable packages, and update the historical security Issue with evidence. Keep the other lockfile only if it is intentionally supported and reproducibly equivalent.

## Acceptance criteria

- Contributors and CI have one documented canonical install command.
- Dependabot monitors the canonical manifest and lockfile.
- The current dependency graph is checked for the historical request vulnerability and remaining high-severity findings.
- Any lockfile change is explained and validated by build and tests.
- No security Issue is closed based only on the absence of a direct dependency.

## Pilot

Perform a clean install and audit from the canonical lockfile, compare the resolved dependency graph with the other lockfile if retained, and record the Dependabot/security result and any remaining transitive path.

## Non-goals

Do not perform broad dependency upgrades without a specific security or compatibility reason.

items.title: [Proposal]: MySQL Package & Extension Manager

labels.name: Extensibility/Ecosystem
labels.description: Extensions, integrations, plugins, and ecosystem opportunities.

items.body:
### Pre-flight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing GitHub issues and did not find a duplicate proposal.
- [x] I have removed or redacted sensitive information.

### Primary Contact Name

Alex Gaetano Padula

### Primary Contact Email

agpadula@tidesdb.com

### Company / Organization

TidesDB Corp.

### Role

Founder, CEO & Chief Architect

### Additional Authors / Contributors

_No response_

### Component

Server

### Target Release (Optional)

MySQL 26.7.0 and later

### Roadmap Section

Extensibility/Ecosystem

### Related Issues / Pull Requests / References (Optional)

_No response_

### Executive Summary

MySQL has one of the broadest extension surfaces of any relational database with eleven and growing implemented
plugin interfaces, pluggable storage engines with real alternatives, loadable functions, and a
component service registry in which one component may re-implement another's service. It has no
distribution mechanism for any of it.

Installing an out-of-tree extension today requires the operator to obtain the MySQL source tree at
the exact version they are running, place the extension inside it, configure and build the whole
server, and copy the resulting shared object into `plugin_dir` by hand. This is not a gap in
tooling; it follows from three properties of the server:

1. *Storage engine plugins are bound to one exact server version.*
   `MYSQL_HANDLERTON_INTERFACE_VERSION` is defined as `(MYSQL_VERSION_ID << 8)`, and
   `sql_plugin.cc` sets both the lower and upper bound of its check from it, so the comparison
   collapses to equality. A plugin built against 26.7.0 is refused by 26.7.1 with *"API version for
   STORAGE ENGINE plugin is too different"*. Patch releases count.
2. *No development headers ship with the server.* An installed 26.7.0 prefix contains only client
   headers (`mysql_com.h`, `errmsg.h`, `field_types.h`, `mysql/`). There is no `handler.h` and no
   `mysql/plugin.h`, so no extension of any kind can be compiled against an installed server.
3. *Plugins can only be loaded from one directory, by bare filename.*
   `INSTALL PLUGIN ... SONAME` passes the library name through `check_valid_path()`, which rejects
   any string containing a directory separator.

This proposal adds the missing layer, a package format, a compatibility key that makes artifact
reuse safe, a resolver that prefers verified pre-built binaries and falls back to building from
source, and a SQL surface for installing, updating and removing packages. It also proposes the two
small server changes without which none of it is possible - shipping the plugin SDK headers, and
publishing the build identity an artifact must match.

Two findings shape this proposals design:

- *Only three of the eleven plugin interfaces are version-locked* (storage engine, daemon,
  information schema). The other eight carry their own interface-version constants that change only
  when that interface changes. A package of a portable kind can be published once and serve many
  server releases, so the expensive per-release build matrix applies to a minority of packages.
- *MySQL's component loader is already scheme-dispatched and the scheme handler is itself a
  replaceable service.* `file://` is implemented, `builtin://` is reserved with no implementation,
  and the loader resolves a scheme by acquiring the service named `dynamic_loader_scheme_<scheme>`.
  A `pkg://` scheme therefore requires no change to the server at all. This has been prototyped and
  works.

### User / Developer Stories

- *As a DBA deploying an alternative storage engine*, I want to install it with one statement
against the server I already run, rather than reproducing the vendor's build environment.

- *As a DBA planning a minor upgrade*, I want to know *before* I upgrade which of my installed
extensions have no artifact for the new server version, because today a 26.7.0 >> 26.7.1 upgrade
silently invalidates every version-locked plugin and the server starts with tables it cannot open.

- *As an extension author*, I want to build against an installed server the way a PostgreSQL
extension author builds against `pg_config`/PGXS, instead of distributing instructions that begin
"clone the MySQL source".

- *As a security-conscious operator*, I want extension installation to be an audited, separately
privileged action against an allow-listed registry with signature verification, rather than "copy
this `.so` into `plugin_dir` as root".

- *As a platform integrator*, I want a declared dependency graph, because real engines are not
self-contained - TideSQL links `libtidesdb` and pins it by major version, and a manager that ignores
native dependencies has solved the easy half of the problem.

- *As a MySQL maintainer*, I want the extension ecosystem to grow without the server taking on
responsibility for third-party code, so the trust boundary and the privilege model must be explicit.

### Proposed Scope

- A package manifest format (_TOML_) describing a package's identity, kind, server compatibility,
  native dependencies, prebuilt artifacts and source build recipe.
- A *compatibility key* - server version, platform, toolchain ABI, build type - that determines
  whether a given artifact may be loaded into a given server.
- A resolver that selects a version satisfying both the request and the server, prefers a verified
  pre-built artifact, and falls back to building from a tagged source checkout.
- Installation support for the extension kinds MySQL already has registries for:
  plugins (`mysql.plugin`), loadable functions (`mysql.func`) and components (`mysql.component`).
- A SQL surface with `INSTALL PACKAGE`, `UPDATE PACKAGE`, `REMOVE PACKAGE`, `SHOW PACKAGES`,
  `SHOW PACKAGE STATUS`.
- A `mysql.package` system table recording, per installed package, the resolved version, the full
  key it was installed for, the constraint originally requested, and the artifact digest.
- A `pkg://` dynamic loader scheme service for components.
- Pre-upgrade compatibility reporting driven by `mysql.package`.
- Two server-side prerequisites - ship the plugin SDK headers and a CMake package; publish the build
  identity (including the numeric version id and the ABI-affecting flag set).

### Out of Scope / Future Work

- *Operating a public registry (maybe on https://planet.mysql.com/)?.* This specifies the client/server mechanism and the manifest format, not who hosts an index or funds a build farm.
- *Packages that carry SQL objects.* PostgreSQL extensions install SQL objects with versioned
  upgrade scripts. That would make loadable-function and information-schema packages considerably
  more useful and is a natural second phase, but it reopens the upgrade-script design question and
  is deliberately excluded here.
- *Sandboxing the build helper beyond process isolation.* A first version runs builds
  out-of-process and unprivileged; container or seccomp confinement is future work.
- *Cross-version artifact compatibility.* Nothing here attempts to create a stable
  storage-engine ABI. The proposal works within the exact-version rule rather than changing it.
- *Automatic rebuild on server upgrade.* The proposal reports and stages; it does not silently
  rebuild extensions during an upgrade.
- *Windows and macOS packaging specifics.* The design is platform-neutral and the key has a
  platform field, but only Linux x86-64 has been exercised in prototypes.

### References

| Source | What it establishes |
|---|---|
| `include/mysql/plugin.h:665` | `MYSQL_HANDLERTON_INTERFACE_VERSION (MYSQL_VERSION_ID << 8)` |
| `include/mysql/plugin.h:115-127` | The twelve plugin type slots; slot 0 (UDF) unimplemented |
| `sql/sql_plugin.cc:404-425,1063` | Per-type version bounds; the "API version … too different" check |
| `sql/sql_plugin.cc:569,664` | `check_valid_path()` rejecting directory separators |
| `components/libminchassis/dynamic_loader.cc:160-205` | URN `scheme://path`; `file://` and reserved `builtin://` |
| `components/libminchassis/dynamic_loader.cc` (`get_scheme_service_from_urn`) | Scheme resolved as `dynamic_loader_scheme_<scheme>` |
| `components/libminchassis/dynamic_loader_scheme_file.cc:160-168` | The duplicate-library guard a scheme must implement |
| `components/libminchassis/registry.cc:256` | `set_default()` a component may re-implement another's service |
| `include/mysql/components/services/dynamic_loader.h:282-303` | The `dynamic_loader_scheme` service definition |
| `scripts/mysql_system_tables.sql:195,203,361` | `mysql.func`, `mysql.plugin`, `mysql.component` |
| `sql/sys_vars.cc:5147-5155` | `version_compile_machine`, `version_compile_os` |

### Functional Requirements

| # | Requirement |
|---|---|
| F1 | A package manifest shall declare name, version, kind, license, server compatibility, native dependencies, zero or more prebuilt artifacts keyed by compatibility key, and an optional source build recipe. |
| F2 | The resolver shall compute the running server's compatibility key from the server itself, not from configuration. |
| F3 | The resolver shall select the highest package version satisfying both the operator's constraint and the server's key; `latest` shall mean *latest compatible*, not latest published. |
| F4 | For a version-locked kind the compatibility specification shall be an exact server version; for a portable kind it shall be a range. |
| F5 | Where a prebuilt artifact matches the key, its digest shall be verified before use, and its manifest signature shall be verified against configured trust roots. |
| F6 | Where no prebuilt artifact matches and source fallback is permitted, the resolver shall obtain the declared source at the declared tag and run the manifest's named build recipe. |
| F7 | Installation shall dispatch by kind `INSTALL PLUGIN` for plugins and storage engines, `CREATE FUNCTION … SONAME` for loadable functions, `INSTALL COMPONENT` for components. |
| F8 | `mysql.package` shall record resolved version, full key, requested constraint, and artifact digest for every installed package. |
| F9 | `UPDATE PACKAGE` shall re-resolve under the *recorded* constraint unless the operator supplies a new one, so an update cannot cross a major boundary implicitly. |
| F10 | The prior artifact shall be retained across an update so a failed load can be rolled back to a known-good file. |
| F11 | Removing a storage engine package shall be refused while tables in that engine exist. |
| F12 | A pre-upgrade check shall resolve every row of `mysql.package` against a nominated target server version and report packages with no matching artifact. |
| F13 | A failed resolution shall report the compatibility key that was sought and the keys that exist, not merely "not found". |
| F14 | Native dependencies declared in `[requires]` shall be resolved, and a missing or incompatible dependency shall fail the install before anything is staged. |


### Non-functional Requirements

| # | Requirement |
|---|---|
| N1 | *No implicit network access.* The registry allow-list shall be empty by default; a server never configured for packages shall not reach the network. |
| N2 | *No unsigned code.* An unsigned package or an unknown signer shall be refused, with no override option. |
| N3 | *Separate privilege.* Package installation shall require its own dynamic privilege, not `SUPER` and not `INSTALL PLUGIN`, default-granted to nobody. |
| N4 | *No compilation inside `mysqld`.* Source builds shall run in a separate unprivileged process with no database access. |
| N5 | *Auditability.* Every install, update and removal shall emit an audit event carrying the resolved key and artifact digest. |
| N6 | *Failure containment.* A failed build or a failed load shall leave the server running and the previous state intact. |
| N7 | *No new steady-state cost.* Resolution runs only on explicit operator action; there shall be no background polling or periodic registry contact. |
| N8 | *Determinism.* Given the same manifest, key and digest, installation shall be reproducible. |


### Impact Areas

- [x] SQL syntax or statements
- [x] Configuration options or system variables
- [x] Command-line options or utilities
- [x] User-visible behavior
- [x] Observability
- [x] Security or privilege model
- [ ] Protocol or replication behavior
- [x] Upgrade / downgrade compatibility
- [ ] Performance or resource usage
- [x] Files, persistence, or metadata formats
- [x] APIs or internal interfaces
- [x] Testing or QA coverage needs

### Summary of the Approach


An extension artifact is addressed by a *compatibility key* with four fields:

```
tidesdb/2.0.0 @ mysql-26.7.0 / linux-x86_64 / gcc13-cxx11abi / release
               └─ server ─┘   └─ platform ─┘   └─ toolchain ─┘  └ build ┘
```

Each field corresponds to a demonstrated failure mode rather than defensive over-specification:

| Field | Why it is in the key |
|---|---|
| `server` | Exact `MYSQL_VERSION_ID` for version-locked kinds; a declared range for portable kinds. |
| `platform` | OS and architecture. |
| `toolchain` | C++ ABI generation and symbol floor. A plugin built on a current Ubuntu requires `GLIBC_2.34` and will not load on RHEL 8 however correct its server version. |
| `build` | Release vs debug. `NDEBUG` changes server struct layouts the extension compiles against. |

Resolution prefers a verified prebuilt artifact and falls back to a source build. The server drives
the operation through SQL; the work of fetching, verifying and building is delegated to a separate
process. Installed state lives in `mysql.package`, which is what makes updates and pre-upgrade
checks possible.

### User Interface

```sql
-- install
INSTALL PACKAGE 'tidesdb';                      -- latest compatible with this server
INSTALL PACKAGE 'tidesdb' VERSION '2.0.0';      -- exact
INSTALL PACKAGE 'tidesdb' VERSION '^2.0';       -- range
INSTALL PACKAGE 'tidesdb' FROM 'vendor-registry';

-- update, re-resolving under the recorded constraint
UPDATE PACKAGE 'tidesdb';
UPDATE PACKAGE 'tidesdb' VERSION '2.1.0';       -- move the constraint deliberately

-- remove
REMOVE PACKAGE 'tidesdb';

-- inspect
SHOW PACKAGES;
SHOW PACKAGE STATUS 'tidesdb';
SELECT * FROM mysql.package;
```

Components additionally become installable through the existing loader with no new syntax, by
registering a scheme service:

```sql
INSTALL COMPONENT 'pkg://some_component@1.2';
```

### Configuration / Knobs


| Variable | Scope | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_registry_allowlist` | Global, dynamic | *empty* | Registries the server may contact. Empty means packages are disabled. |
| `package_trust_roots` | Global, startup | *empty* | Public keys that may sign manifests and artifacts. Never read from a registry. |
| `package_store_dir` | Global, startup | `<basedir>/pkg` | Where verified component artifacts are staged. |
| `package_allow_source_build` | Global, dynamic | `OFF` | Whether the source fallback may run on this host. |
| `package_build_timeout` | Global, dynamic | 600 s | Upper bound on a source build. |

New read-only variables publishing the build identity (prerequisite, see §5):

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `version_id` | The numeric `MYSQL_VERSION_ID` the plugin loader actually compares. *Not currently exposed* - only `@@version` as a string, which may carry a suffix. |
| `build_toolchain` | Compiler and C++ ABI tag the server was built with. |
| `build_type` | `release` / `debug`. |
| `sdk_cxxflags`, `sdk_ldflags` | The ABI-affecting flag set an extension must be built with. |

### Observability

- *`mysql.package`* - one row per installed package >> name, resolved version, kind, compatibility
  key, requested constraint, artifact digest, install timestamp, source (`binary` or `source`).
- *`SHOW PACKAGE STATUS <name>`* - resolved version against available versions, whether an update
  is available under the recorded constraint, and whether a staged-but-pending artifact exists.
- *Audit events* - one per install, update and removal, carrying resolved key and digest, so
  extension installation is reviewable after the fact.
- *Error log* - resolution failures name the key sought and the keys available; build failures
  include the helper's captured output, truncated.
- *Performance Schema (optional)* - stages for `resolve`, `fetch`, `verify`, `build`, `stage`,
  `load`, so a slow install is attributable.


### User Procedure


Installing an engine on a server that has a matching prebuilt artifact:

```sql
mysql> SET GLOBAL package_registry_allowlist = 'https://pkg.example';
mysql> GRANT INSTALL_PACKAGE ON *.* TO 'dba'@'localhost';
mysql> INSTALL PACKAGE 'tidesdb';
mysql> SELECT * FROM mysql.package;
mysql> CREATE TABLE t (id INT PRIMARY KEY) ENGINE=TidesDB;
```

Preparing for a server upgrade:

```sql
mysql> SHOW PACKAGE STATUS FOR SERVER '26.7.1';
+---------+---------+------------------+--------------------------------+
| package | version | target_available | note                           |
+---------+---------+------------------+--------------------------------+
| tidesdb | 2.0.0   | NO               | no artifact for mysql-26.7.1   |
| connlog | 1.0.0   | YES              | portable kind, range satisfied |
+---------+---------+------------------+--------------------------------+
```

The operator stages the new-key artifacts before upgrading, so the upgraded server finds its
extensions already present rather than starting with unloadable plugins.

### Security Considerations


Server-driven installation is the most useful shape and the most dangerous. It gives `mysqld`
outbound network access and, on the source path, a compiler. Four containments, all mandatory:

1. *Trust.* Manifests and artifacts are signed; the server verifies against trust roots configured
   at startup, never material supplied by the registry. An unsigned or unknown-signer package is
   refused with *no override flag* - an override becomes the documented workaround.
2. *Privilege.* `INSTALL_PACKAGE` is its own dynamic privilege, default-granted to nobody, and is
   not implied by `SUPER` or `INSTALL PLUGIN`. Installing a package is strictly more dangerous than
   loading a file an administrator already placed on the host.
3. *Network.* `package_registry_allowlist` is empty by default. There is no implicit default
   registry, so a server that is never configured for packages cannot be induced to fetch anything.
4. *Build isolation.* The source path never compiles inside `mysqld`. `mysql_package_build` runs
   as a separate unprivileged process with no database connection, a scratch directory, and the
   named recipe from the manifest. On hosts with no toolchain the helper is absent and the source
   path reports that plainly.

Residual risks that should be stated rather than designed away, a signed package is still arbitrary
code in the server's address space; the registry operator is a trusted party; and the build helper
executes a recipe from a manifest, which is why `package_allow_source_build` defaults off and why a
binary-only first version is a reasonable scope reduction.

### Compatibility and Behavior Changes

- *No change to existing extension loading.* `INSTALL PLUGIN`, `CREATE FUNCTION … SONAME` and
  `INSTALL COMPONENT 'file://…'` behave exactly as before.
- *New system table.* `mysql.package` requires a dictionary upgrade step. A downgrade leaves the
  table present and unused.
- *The plugin SDK becomes a published interface.* This is the significant new commitment, once
  headers ship, their contents become something third parties build against. The SDK should
  therefore carry its own version and an explicit stability statement - in particular that it offers
  *no* cross-version guarantee for the version-locked kinds, matching the loader's existing rule.
- *Replication.* Unaffected; package state is local to a server.
- *Upgrade hazard addressed, not introduced.* A server version change already invalidates every
  version-locked extension. This proposal makes that visible and recoverable instead of leaving it
  to be discovered at startup.


### Block Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["INSTALL PACKAGE 'tidesdb'"] --> B["Privilege check: INSTALL_PACKAGE"]
    B --> C["Read compatibility key from this server"]
    C --> D["Resolve version: constraint AND server compat"]
    D --> E["Verify manifest signature against trust roots"]
    E --> F["Resolve native dependencies from [requires]"]
    F --> G{"Prebuilt artifact<br/>for this key?"}
    G -- yes --> H["Verify sha256"]
    G -- no --> I{"package_allow_source_build?"}
    I -- no --> J["Fail: report key sought + keys available"]
    I -- yes --> K["mysql_package_build:<br/>unprivileged, no DB access"]
    K --> L["Run named recipe against SDK"]
    L --> H
    H --> M["Stage into plugin_dir or package_store_dir"]
    M --> N{"kind"}
    N -- "plugin / storage_engine" --> O["INSTALL PLUGIN"]
    N -- loadable_function --> P["CREATE FUNCTION ... SONAME"]
    N -- component --> Q["INSTALL COMPONENT 'pkg://name'"]
    O --> R["Record in mysql.package + audit event"]
    P --> R
    Q --> R
```

### Interface Specification

*Manifest format.* TOML, one file per package version.

```toml
[package]
name        = "tidesdb"
version     = "2.0.0"
kind        = "storage_engine"      # selects the version-locking rule
plugin_name = "TidesDB"          # what INSTALL PLUGIN registers
soname      = "ha_tidesdb.so"
license     = "GPL-2.0"
maturity    = "beta"

[compat]
server = "=26.7.0"               # exact storage engines are version-locked
                                            # an audit plugin would write server = ">=8.0.0"

[requires]
libtidesdb = "^10.1.1"           # native dependency, major pinned

[[binary]]
key    = "mysql-26.7.0/linux-x86_64/gcc13-cxx11abi/release"
url    = "https://pkg.example/tidesdb/2.0.0/…"
sha256 = "…"

# for multiplatform / architecture 
[[binary]]
key    = "mysql-26.7.0/linux-aarch64/gcc13-cxx11abi/release"
url    = "https://pkg.example/tidesdb/2.0.0/linux-aarch64.so"
sha256 = "…"

[[binary]]
key    = "mysql-26.7.0/macos-arm64/clang17-libc++/release"
url    = "…"
key    = "mysql-26.7.0/macos-arm64/clang17-libc++/release"
url    = "…"
sha256 = "…"

[[binary]]
key    = "mysql-26.7.0/windows-x64/msvc193/release"
url    = "…"
sha256 = "…"

[source]
git      = "https://github.com/tidesdb/tidesql-mysql"
tag      = "v2.0.0"
build    = "./install.sh --rebuild-plugin --mysql-src ${MYSQL_SDK_SRC}"
produces = "ha_tidesdb.so"
```

`kind` is what lets the resolver apply the right version rule without the manifest restating it.
`[source]` is a *named recipe*, not an arbitrary shell string, so the build helper has something it
can constrain.

*`mysql.package` system table.*

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `varchar(64)` PK | Package name |
| `version` | `varchar(32)` | Resolved version |
| `kind` | `varchar(32)` | `storage_engine`, `plugin`, `loadable_function`, `component` |
| `compat_key` | `varchar(255)` | Full key the artifact was installed for |
| `constraint_spec` | `varchar(64)` | Constraint originally requested |
| `artifact_sha256` | `char(64)` | Digest of the staged artifact |
| `origin` | `enum('binary','source')` | How it was acquired |
| `installed_at` | `timestamp` | Install time |
| `pending_version` | `varchar(32)` NULL | Staged update awaiting restart |

*The `pkg://` scheme service.* No core change is required. The loader resolves a scheme by name:

```c
/* components/libminchassis/dynamic_loader.cc, get_scheme_service_from_urn */
size_t scheme_end = urn.find("://");
my_string scheme(urn.begin(), urn.begin() + scheme_end);
my_service<SERVICE_TYPE(dynamic_loader_scheme)> service(
    (my_string("dynamic_loader_scheme_") + scheme).c_str(),
    &imp_mysql_minimal_chassis_registry);
```

A component providing `dynamic_loader_scheme_pkg` therefore extends a *running* server. The service
name is declared as an alias of the service type, exactly as the built-in file scheme does:

```c
typedef SERVICE_TYPE_NO_CONST(dynamic_loader_scheme)
    SERVICE_TYPE_NO_CONST(dynamic_loader_scheme_pkg);

BEGIN_SERVICE_IMPLEMENTATION(pkg_scheme, dynamic_loader_scheme_pkg)
pkg_load, pkg_unload END_SERVICE_IMPLEMENTATION();
```

> The scheme contract carries an invariant the service definition does not express. The
> definition is only `load` and `unload`, but a scheme implementation *must* refuse to load the
> same library twice. The built-in file scheme guards on the address of the library's
> `list_components` entry point (`dynamic_loader_scheme_file.cc:160-168`); without that guard the
> same component is registered twice and the second unload frees state the first still references.
> A first prototype that omitted it crashed the server with SIGSEGV. If the scheme mechanism is to
> be opened to third parties, this contract must be specified, or a helper supplied that enforces
> it.

*The plugin SDK.* Measured from the compiler's own dependency output, not estimated:

```
storage engine header closure          366 headers,  5.1 MB
  include/ 188   sql/ 97   libs/ 69   sql-common/ 4   extra/ 4   vector-common/ 1
  generated 3 - my_config.h, mysql_version.h, mysqld_error.h   (configuration-specific)

+ component service headers           +161 headers
union across extension kinds              527 headers
```

Three properties of the SDK follow:

1. `libmysqlservices.a` already ships. It supplies `mysql_malloc_service` and
   `plugin_registry_service`, and is already installed into the prefix. Only the headers are
   missing, which makes this ask smaller than it appears.
2. The flag set is part of the ABI. A complete engine compiled and linked cleanly but would not
   load until built with the server's own `-ftls-model=initial-exec`, `-D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64` and
   `-Wl,-Bsymbolic-functions`. Publishing a toolchain *tag* is insufficient; the flags themselves
   must be published.
3. The SDK must be a union, not a sample. The storage-engine closure appeared to be a superset -
   it already contained `plugin_audit.h`, `udf_registration_types.h` and
   `component_implementation.h` - yet a component failed to compile, because a storage engine never
   includes any `components/services/*.h`.


### Proposed Implementation Plan


The ordering is chosen so that each phase is independently useful and the riskiest work comes last.

| Phase | Work item | Server change | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ship the plugin SDK, 527 headers, the generated configuration headers, and a CMake package for out-of-tree builds. Publish the SDK's own version and stability statement. | Install rules + packaging | Prerequisite; validated by building a complete storage engine, an audit plugin, a loadable function and a component against a staged SDK with no source tree |
| 2 | Publish the build identity with numeric `version_id`, toolchain tag, build type, and the ABI-affecting compile/link flag set as read-only variables. | New read-only sysvars | Gap confirmed - no numeric version id is currently exposed |
| 3 | `pkg://` dynamic loader scheme service, shipped as a component, plus a written scheme contract or an enforcement helper. | None | **Prototyped and working**; a component installed through `pkg://` appears in `mysql.component` |
| 4 | `mysql.package` system table, the `INSTALL_PACKAGE` dynamic privilege, audit events, and the configuration variables. | Dictionary + privilege + sysvars | Designed |
| 5 | Parser and runtime for `INSTALL/UPDATE/REMOVE PACKAGE` and `SHOW PACKAGE[S]`, binary path only (verified prebuilt artifacts). | Parser + runtime | Resolution logic prototyped client-side |
| 6 | `mysql_package_build` helper and the source fallback, behind `package_allow_source_build=OFF`. | New helper binary | Prototyped client-side - git clone at tag >> build against SDK >> stage >> install |
| 7 | Pre-upgrade compatibility reporting (`SHOW PACKAGE STATUS FOR SERVER`). | Runtime | Designed |


### QA Notes


### Correctness and refusal paths

| Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|
| Install a version-locked package whose artifact key names a different server patch release | Refused before staging, naming the key sought and the keys available |
| Artifact digest does not match the manifest | Refused; nothing staged |
| Manifest unsigned, or signed by a key not in `package_trust_roots` | Refused; no override path exists |
| Registry not in `package_registry_allowlist` | Refused without network contact |
| `package_allow_source_build=OFF` and no binary matches | Refused with a clear reason, not a silent build |
| Source build exits non-zero, times out, or produces no artifact | Statement fails; server unaffected; previous state intact |
| `REMOVE PACKAGE` for a storage engine with live tables | Refused - requires asking the engine, not the file system |
| `UPDATE PACKAGE` where the newest version violates the recorded constraint | No update performed; reported as already current |
| Update whose new artifact fails to load | Rolls back to the retained previous artifact |
| Install a package already installed | Idempotent or clearly refused; never double-registered |

### Scheme-specific

| Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|
| Same library loaded via `file://` and `pkg://` | Second load refused by the duplicate-library guard |
| `pkg://` URN naming an absent artifact | Clean failure, no crash |
| `UNINSTALL COMPONENT` then reinstall through the same URN | Succeeds; no stale registration |
| Scheme component unloaded while a `pkg://` component is loaded | Defined behaviour required; currently undefined |

### Cross-version and upgrade

| Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|
| Start a server one patch release newer with version-locked packages installed | Pre-upgrade check lists them; post-upgrade repair path reports them rather than failing silently |
| Staged `pending_version` applied at restart | New artifact loads; `mysql.package` updated |
| Downgrade below the version that created `mysql.package` | Table unused; no errors |

### Automation opportunities

- The refusal matrix above is mostly table-driven and suits `mysql-test-run` with a fixture registry
  served from the test's own directory, no network needed.
- Cross-version refusal can be tested without a second server build by publishing a manifest whose
  artifact key names a fabricated version; the loader's check is what is under test.
- The duplicate-library guard deserves a dedicated crash-regression test, since it is an invariant
  a third-party scheme must honour and a prototype has already violated it.
- Digest and signature failures should be tested with deliberately corrupted artifacts rather than
  mocks, since the whole value of the key is that it is checked against reality.

### Known gaps in current validation

- Only Linux x86-64 has been exercised. The platform and toolchain fields of the key are designed but
  untested on macOS and Windows.
- Signature verification is specified but not implemented in the prototype; only digests are checked.
- The server-driven surface (`INSTALL PACKAGE`) is designed and not implemented; the prototype drives
  installation from a client, which is the same resolution logic in a different process.
- `libtidesdb`-style native dependency resolution is declared in the manifest format and checked for
  presence only; version-range satisfaction across a dependency graph is not implemented.

items.title: [core-split] Retire bitty-package distribution semantics into bitty-plugin-manager
items.body:
Priority: P1 | Area: architecture | Labels: chore,P1,area:architecture | Milestone: v0.1.0 | Audit: bitty#1629 (CTX-1085 Slice A/B)

## Summary

Retire the draft package-lifecycle capability living in Core (`bitty-package`
resolver/trust/lockfile/catalog/source, the 7-stage `verify_install`
pipeline, the `bitty plugin install|remove|enable|...` CLI, and host-side
dependency version solving) into `bitty-plugin-manager` once its registry
index + version-constraint solving land (manager#11). Core keeps only
manifest parse, startup re-verification, and the in-memory lifecycle
registry mechanism.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/bitty-package/src/{resolver,activation,trust,lockfile,integrity,catalog,source}.rs`
  (~3700 loc): version solving, generation-ring activation/rollback, Ed25519
  publisher trust (V-A/V-B/V-C), lockfile digest triple. Self-labelled
  "draft / not normative".
- `crates/bitty-plugin-host/src/install.rs:187-237`: 7-stage install-time
  verification (fetch framing, checksums, capability diff, TOFU pinning,
  signed verify).
- `crates/bitty-terminal/src/plugin.rs:1-45`: full package-manager CLI
  (`install|remove|enable|disable|revoke|info`) with `git` sources disabled
  as "package-manager follow-up".
- `crates/bitty-plugin-host/src/registry.rs` (`resolve_all`,
  `service_version_satisfies`): dependency-graph resolution + interface
  version solving.
- `crates/bitty-package/src/source.rs`: `PackageSource::Registry { url }`
  grammar + `git+ssh://` scheme policy (manager-side policy text).

## Target state

- Trust, resolver + version solving, lockfile, catalog, registry grammar,
  and the install verification pipeline move to `bitty-plugin-manager`
  via its #10/#11 surface (migration boundary already published there).
- `bitty plugin ...` becomes a thin client delegating via trait/CLI handoff.
- Core retains: manifest parse + schema/compat validation, startup
  integrity/compatibility/grant re-verification, in-memory lifecycle
  registry as mechanism.
- The component-install seed (bitty#1791, shipped) stays as the bootstrap
  and is not duplicated: it installs the manager, then hands off.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No dependency solving, version solving, publisher-trust, lockfile,
      or catalog code remains in Core (`rg` clean for the moved modules).
- [ ] `bitty plugin install|remove|enable|disable|revoke|info` delegate to
      the manager; local-path behavior unchanged and fail-closed.
- [ ] `just check` + `just ci-local` green; Windows `--target` check green.
- [ ] Docs synced (`bitty-terminal-docs` platform material if behavior
      changes; manager repo owns the moved contracts).

## Dependencies / blockers

- `bitty-plugin-manager#11` (registry index + version-constraint solving)
  must land first; manager#10 is closed. Seed/manager overlap tracked from
  bitty#1629; do not duplicate the seed.

## Scheduling

Post-0.0.23 work. Land inside the 0.0.24 window (milestone stays v0.1.0).
No implementation until a CarryCtx task is claimed; this issue is the
立案 record only.

items.title: build(deps): upgrade pnpm 10 to 12 once the dependency graph reads its lockfile
items.body:
## Outcome

The repository uses pnpm 12 (`packageManager`, CI, Docker images, and desk images). GitHub's dependency graph, Dependency Review, and Dependabot security alerts still see every dependency.

## Blocked by

GitHub's dependency graph reads the two-document `pnpm-lock.yaml` that pnpm 11 and 12 write (an environment document from `packageManager`, then the dependency graph) as zero dependencies: [dependabot-core#15904](https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core/issues/15904), open, and GitHub support confirmed it on 2026-10-21. The only workaround, `pmOnFail: ignore`, turns off the pnpm version check. Start this work when that issue is fixed.

## Acceptance criteria

- `package.json` `packageManager`, `PNPM_VERSION` in every workflow, `pnpm/action-setup`, `Dockerfile.api`, `Dockerfile.web`, and `tooling/desk/docker/desk.Dockerfile` all name the same pnpm 12 version.
- `.npmrc` keeps only registry and auth settings; `shared-workspace-lockfile`, `prefer-workspace-packages`, `auto-install-peers`, and `strict-peer-dependencies` move to `pnpm-workspace.yaml` in camelCase.
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` has an `allowBuilds` map, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes with pnpm's default `strictDepBuilds: true`.
- `minimumReleaseAge`, `overrides`, `patchedDependencies`, `auditConfig.ignoreGhsas`, and both catalogs still apply (`pnpm install` resolves the same versions; `pnpm audit` honors the ignores).
- The self-hosted runner store variable is `pnpm_config_store_dir` (pnpm 11 stopped reading `npm_config_*`): `tooling/ci-runners/scale-set.values.yaml`, `.github/actions/setup-node-pnpm/action.yml`, `docs/self-hosted-ci.md`.
- On the PR, the Dependency Review job reports dependencies, and the repository dependency graph lists the npm dependencies after merge.
- The `Install dependencies` step time in CI is reported against the 5.5 s baseline below.

## Scope

Root `package.json`, `.npmrc`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `.github/actions/setup-node-pnpm`, `Dockerfile.*`, `tooling/desk/docker`, `tooling/desk/src/isolation/docker.image.ts`, `scripts/doctor.mjs`, `tooling/ci-runners`, `docs/self-hosted-ci.md`, `README.md`, `.ai/serena-memories/environment_setup.md`.

## Validation

Tier: pre-PR. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm smoke`, `pnpm desk doctor`; both Docker images build in CI.

## Evidence

- `package.json:5` pins `pnpm@10.29.3`. pnpm 12.0.0 (Rust rewrite, same lockfile format) is stable since 2026-08-26. The latest is 12.15.0.
- CI run 40320609082, Check Fast: `pnpm install` took 5.5 s, and the `actions/setup-node` pnpm store restore (280 MB) took 8.6 s. pnpm 12 shortens only the first part.
- `tooling/ci-runners/scale-set.values.yaml:84` and `.github/actions/setup-node-pnpm/action.yml:54` use `npm_config_store_dir`.
- Dependabot supports pnpm 11 and 12 since 2026-10-20 ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-20-dependabot-now-supports-npm-12-pnpm-11-and-12-and-bun-1-4/)). The dependency graph does not yet ([dependabot-core#15904](https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core/issues/15904)).

## Out of scope

- Bun or any other package manager (ADR 0017).
- `pmOnFail: ignore` as a workaround: it removes the pnpm version check.

## Origin

CI and tooling performance review, 2026-10-26 (ADR 0017).

items.title: Align Snyk gateway project with the actual pnpm workspace dependency graph
items.body:
API foundation PR tarkovtracker-org/TarkovTracker#1145 has a failed Snyk npm-manifest project check reporting Undici 7.29.0 through Wrangler/Miniflare, although the actual workspace and isolated standalone installs resolve only patched Undici 7.30.0.

Fresh evidence at `68c567a4fa3de4d1259017132bfd38c23b1bbaa4`:
- Frozen pnpm install; `pnpm --filter api-gateway why undici`: only 7.30.0.
- `pnpm run verify:api-standalone`: 112 rules and 297 gateway tests pass, type/boundary/generated-type/OpenAPI/build checks pass; isolated installed graph also has only Undici 7.30.0.
- `pnpm run audit:dependencies`: passes unchanged production gate. Full audit has no Undici advisory; separately tracked development-tool advisories are not suppressed.
- Current Snyk check: https://app.snyk.io/org/tarkovtracker-org/pr-checks/970826d1-855c-4502-af8d-df3978b45856 . The report remains failed; no advisory/check was dismissed, overridden or marked successful.

Snyk documents that nested npm manifests without a neighboring lockfile are approximated without the root lockfile: https://docs.snyk.io/supported-languages/supported-languages-list/javascript . This is consistent with the reported mismatched graph.

Resolution: retain scanning of the actual root pnpm workspace and configure the gateway project to consume its real lockfile/graph. Validate that the scanner reports installed Undici 7.30.0, retains security/dev-dependency coverage, and rerun its check. Do not add ignore rules, duplicate package-manager lockfiles, or disable security controls. This environment has GitHub access but no authenticated Snyk API/CLI access, so the project configuration cannot be repaired here. Production cutover remains separate.

items.title: architecture: no dependency graph shows the edges and cycles between modules

milestone.title: M2 · Architecture measured
milestone.description:
Numbers decide what the architecture skill keeps, before more is built on it.

Done when the eval of #99 prints, for each of its four arms, the runs that use the existing wrapper, and #87 records the decision those numbers give: keep the skill, cut it to the ADR rules, or remove it.

Current.

items.body:
Part of #87.

## Why

A graph of the imports between modules gives:

- the codemap of a first `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (#96): the modules and the direction of their dependencies;
- the edges and the cycles that a branch adds, for the review lens (#97): the graph at the base against the graph at the head;
- the cycles and the broken layers, for debt (#98);
- invariants of the form "A does not import B": a third kind of `Check:` line in `invariants.sh` (#96).

Decided with the person: a soft dependency. Where a tool runs for the language, use it. Where none does, skip it and say so.

## Candidates

Researched on 2026-10-25. Activity and releases from the GitHub API and the package registries.

- **codebase-memory-mcp** 0.12.1 (MIT, 2026-10-16): 162 languages through tree-sitter, with no build and no language server. `npx codebase-memory-mcp@0.12.1` downloads its binary and checks its SHA-256. A plain CLI prints JSON: `IMPORTS` edges through a read-only `query_graph`, cycles, and `compare_graphs`. Risks: it is at 0.x, so its JSON can change; each run downloads a binary and starts a temporary daemon; how well it resolves TS path aliases and Python `src` layouts is not checked.
- **Per language**, each with no build and no code of the project:
  - `package.json`: dependency-cruiser 18.7.0, with `--no-config`, and `--ts-config` for path aliases;
  - Python: `ruff analyze graph` (ruff 0.17.2; it prints an "experimental" warning);
  - `go.mod`: `go list -json`.

  Rust, Java/Kotlin, PHP, C# and Ruby get no graph: cargo-modules runs build scripts and proc macros, jdeps and ArchUnit need a build, deptrac needs Composer and PHP.
- **Left out:** madge and aider's repo map (last releases in 2024 and 2025), GitNexus (a non-commercial license), Serena and narsil-mcp (MCP only), the SCIP indexers (scip-java runs the build).

## What to change

1. A trial on a fixture: codebase-memory-mcp against dependency-cruiser, on a TS tree with path aliases. Compare their edges.
2. The same edges: take codebase-memory-mcp. More missing or wrong edges: take the set per language.
3. `graph.sh <tree>` in the shape of `skills/debt/scripts/clones.sh`: a pinned version in a private directory, on a copy of the code files, the cache in its own temporary directory, no package manager and no script of the project in the project's tree. Each tool has its own runner: `npx` or `bunx` for codebase-memory-mcp and dependency-cruiser; `uvx ruff@<pin>` for ruff; the `go` on `PATH` with `GOPROXY=off` and `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` for `go list`. With no runner, that tool is skipped. dependency-cruiser runs through `npx` only, with a pinned `typescript` beside it (without it, it reads no `.ts` file; `bunx` keeps only the last `-p`, so with no `npx` it is skipped with a line), and with `--no-config`, so the project's `.dependency-cruiser.js`, which the copy holds as code, never loads. It gets `--ts-config` when the copy has a `tsconfig.json`; when it fails on that file, as on an `extends` of a package or a generated file, it runs again without it and prints a line that the edges through path aliases are missing. Unlike `clones.sh`, the copy keeps the files that the tools read as data and that `data.ere` leaves out: each `tsconfig*.json` (one can extend another), `go.sum`, `pyproject.toml`. `go.mod` is code to `data.ere`, so the copy has it already. The trial gives both tools the same copy. It prints the edges folded to directories, as JSON. With no tool for the language, it prints `skipped: <why>` and exits 0.
4. `invariants.sh` gets the kind "A does not import B", from those edges.

## Change coupling

items.title: Read OpenWrt opkg package databases

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
OpenWrt and its many derivatives (vendor router firmware, prplOS, Turris OS, GL.iNet's and others) record installed packages with opkg. Newer OpenWrt releases are moving to APK, which cdxgen already reads. Trivy does not read opkg databases, so today a scan of an OpenWrt root filesystem finds almost nothing from the package manager, even though the information is sitting in plain text.

cdxgen should read `/usr/lib/opkg/status` and the per-package `/usr/lib/opkg/info/*.control` files (on some systems they live under `/var/lib/opkg`), and produce a component for each installed package. The component should carry the version, architecture, source package (`Source:`), license (`License:`), maintainer, dependencies (`Depends:`, which give a real dependency graph), the ABI version and the installed file list from `*.list`. Packages marked as part of the base image (ROM) should be distinguished from those installed later (overlay), which OpenWrt tracks with the `Status:` and `Installed-Time` fields.

The package URL needs a decision. The purl specification has no `opkg` type today. Candidates are `pkg:generic/openwrt/<name>@<version>?arch=...` with a distribution qualifier, or a proposal to the purl specification for a proper type. Decide in this issue, and record whichever is chosen in `docs/CUSTOM_PROPERTIES.md` so that vulnerability tools can rely on it. Add CPEs only for packages whose upstream identity is clear (for example `dropbear`, `dnsmasq` and `busybox`), using a small mapping table rather than guessing.

Tests: an OpenWrt x86-64 release image from the corpus, where the package list must match `opkg list-installed` run inside the image under QEMU at corpus build time; a status file with ROM and overlay packages; and malformed control files.

Done when OpenWrt images produce one component per installed package with dependencies, licences and files, and the purl choice is documented.

items.title: Reuse validated immutable dependency graphs across Deployments without recreating and deleting node_modules
items.body:
## What

At `7fa6242`, dependency preparation is reused only within one immutable workspace. Each changed-Commit deploy, Preview creation, force deploy and rollback receives a new workspace and invokes installation again even when dependency inputs are identical (`src/adapters/target-effects.ts:583–611`; `src/runtime/preparation.ts:40–43`; `src/runtime/targets.ts:146–150`). Reclamation then traverses and removes that revision's entire dependency tree.

This is an opt-in performance opportunity, not a claim that Rig downloads packages on every deploy. **Bun already reuses its package cache and defaults to clonefile installation on macOS.** The missing reuse is a validated complete installed graph between Deployment workspaces, including its directory metadata and preparation receipt.

## Numbers and method

Ordinary performance QA on b-mini, Bun 1.4.2, APFS, read-only audit `7fa6242f4911c043637e480e8b394c369607491a`. A synthetic loopback HTTP Project uses the audit checkout's actual `package.json` and `bun.lock`, yielding **25,372 files / 521.71 MiB** of `node_modules`. Existing cached packages were APFS-copied into a separate `/tmp` package cache; no packages were downloaded and the user's cache was not changed.

A `/tmp` PATH wrapper records the automatic install invocation and elapsed time, then executes the real Bun binary with the arguments Rig requested plus `--offline --cache-dir <temporary cache>`. It does not fake the installation. Project `environment.PATH` selects that wrapper; every Rig/rigd shell exported its isolated `RIG_ROOT`. No proxy or launchd was involved.

- First deploy **2.013 s**; one-line second deploy **4.279 s**.
- Stable changed-Commit deploys 2–10 **4.266–4.537 s**, median **4.356 s**.
- Preview create **1.849 s**; exact first-Commit rollback through `/v1/command` **4.091 s**; Preview destroy **4.452 s**.
- The wrapper recorded **12 actual installs**: ten stable deploys, Preview creation and rollback. Every package/lockfile stayed byte-for-byte identical. Installs took **0.782–0.881 s**, around **0.81 s** each.
- Ten stable deploys retain one complete dependency tree; root allocation increases only **220 KiB** from deploy 1 to 10. There is no recurrence of #153's unbounded revision leak.
- A prepared checkout is **521.87 MiB allocated by du**; Preview creation adds another. During rollback with a Preview, old stable + candidate + Preview temporarily coexist (about **1.53 GiB** of dependency-tree du allocation). APFS may share data extents: these du totals are not unique physical storage measurements.
- An installed `next` file and its temp-cache source have identical content, distinct inodes and `nlink=1`; this agrees with clonefile-backed independent files, not hardlinks. The automatic command still runs and recreates the installed directory graph.
- Filesystem control: copying the existing complete tree with `cp -R` took **26.38 s**, `cp -cR` **9.88 s**, versus about **0.81 s** for real warm offline Bun install. These are shared-host single samples. A Rig-level cache which just clones the complete tree would be **worse than Bun's current installer** here.
- Isolated registered-worktree control: cloning the installed tree took **6.273 s**; `git worktree remove --force` plus prune took **2.223 s**. This separates dependency-tree reclamation from HTTP Service activation.
- A separate probe linked an already prepared complete tree into a new scratch workspace in **0.000109 s**; `require("next/package.json").version` and `require.resolve("next")` succeeded. This is only a narrow resolution proof, not a generally safe shared-tree implementation.

Executable probes and wrapper-generation method: `/tmp/rig-40b-bench.py`, `/tmp/rig-40b-native-cache.py`, `/tmp/rig-40b-native-validate.py`, `/tmp/rig-40b-dep-release.py`. Small evidence is retained in `/tmp/rig-40b-report/`; large fixture data is removed after isolated rigd uninstall.

## How to reproduce

1. Create a fresh `/tmp` root with `dashboard: false`; export `RIG_ROOT` in every shell, install source rigd from the audit checkout, and register a scratch Project with stable and preview enabled.
2. Copy the audit `package.json` and `bun.lock` into the Project. Seed a temporary Bun cache from already installed matching package-cache directories. Use a PATH wrapper for `bun install` that records time and adds `--offline --cache-dir <temp cache>`, forwarding all other calls unchanged.
3. Commit, deploy and measure. Make nine one-line changes to an unrelated tracked text file, committing and deploying each. Leave dependency inputs unchanged. Count wrapper calls and collect revision directories and `du -sk` after each deploy.
4. Deploy a non-production Branch as a Preview, exact-Commit roll back stable through the isolated control plane, then destroy the Preview. Verify installation ran again for each.
5. Compare whole-tree copy and clone costs separately. To isolate reclamation, materialize a scratch registered worktree anchored to a separate Rig-style mirror, populate its dependency tree from the stopped prepared fixture, and time `git worktree remove --force` followed by prune. Never modify or release a managed checkout from this probe.
6. Stop stable and uninstall the isolated daemon before deleting fixture data.

## Why it matters and suggested direction

Avoiding the automatic install alone would save only about **0.81 s / 19%** of the measured 4.36 s warm deploy, because Bun already has an efficient clonefile package cache. The bigger opportunity is avoiding complete installed-graph recreation **and** per-revision traversal/deletion when dependency inputs are unchanged. Keep that distinction visible instead of adding a slow full-tree copy cache. The isolated remove measurement plus installation totals about **3.03 s**; eliminating that work suggests a warm deploy could fall from **4.36 s to about 1.3–1.5 s** (roughly **3×**), plus any new cache-validation cost. This is an estimate, not an implemented end-to-end result.

Investigate an **explicitly opt-in**, separately owned prepared-dependency store keyed by lockfile, manifests, local/workspace dependency content, package-manager version, architecture and every declared install-affecting input. Projects eligible for immutable graph sharing could reference one complete graph across Deployments; otherwise preserve today's independently mutable trees or reuse an eligible idle workspace (#635). Count references durably and reclaim unused cache entries under count/byte budgets. Never hardlink mutable installed files between running Targets.

The small linking probe establishes filesystem feasibility only. Install scripts, workspace links, path-sensitive generated files, environment changes, package-manager differences and dependencies that write into their install directories must be part of eligibility/invalidation. Build outputs must remain isolated, and a failed install must never publish a cache entry.

## Done when

An opt-in immutable-dependency fixture proves warm deploys, new Previews and rollback reuse a validated complete graph with no installer invocation and no full graph deletion per revision. An invalidating lockfile/manifest/environment/platform/local-package change produces fresh preparation; failed or uncertain installation cannot be reused. Default mutable-project behavior remains correct, retention is bounded, and an end-to-end benchmark reports the actual gain over Bun's existing package cache.
